result:
Existing test suite is unaffected and still passes. Summary of what I did:

- Explored the existing test conventions (`ParserTestCase.java`, `DefaultParserTest.java`, `pom.xml` → JUnit 4.12, `org.junit.Test`/static `org.junit.Assert.*` style) and read `DefaultParser.java` plus its collaborators (`CommandLine`, `Options`, `OptionGroup`, `OptionBuilder`, and the exception hierarchy) to know the public API surface.
- Wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/cli/DefaultParserAgentTest.java` with 42 self-contained test methods covering: all four `parse(...)` overloads, short/long option parsing, `--` termination, missing-argument/missing-required-option(s)/unrecognized-option/ambiguous-option/already-selected exceptions (asserting on their getters and messages), option groups (selection, reset across reused `Options`, required groups), negative numbers and hyphen-prefixed values, `=`-style and bursted short options, Java-property-style options (`-Dk=v`), unlimited-arg options, and the `Properties` overlay behavior (defaults, precedence, unrecognized keys, group interaction).
- Verified with `defects4j compile` (success) and ran the new test class standalone (42/42 pass) as well as the pre-existing `DefaultParserTest` (58/58 pass, unaffected).
